description: All ChatHealthy.ai corporate and governance policies. Single source of truth for policies. Engineering operating rules are a separate collection (operating_rules.json) established as a binding standard by GOV-007.

ai_governance.title: ChatHealthy AI Governance Policy
ai_governance.policy_core: The model may suggest. The system must decide.
ai_governance.core_principle: Token prediction ≠ truth. All AI-generated output is probabilistic language, not verified fact. No system behavior may treat model output as authoritative truth.

ai_model.role: Translate user language into structured signals, suggest possible mappings, generate explanations
constraints: MUST NOT introduce new facts outside system data
MUST NOT be treated as a source of truth

data_layer.role: Single source of truth. All factual, auditable information. Derived from verified public or consented sources.
constraints: All outputs must trace back to this layer
No model-generated data may overwrite or augment it

decision_layer.role: Apply rules, mappings, and scoring. Determine bounded outputs. Enforce constraints and guardrails.
constraints: MUST NOT defer decision authority to the model

explanation_layer.role: Present results in clear, user-friendly language. Describe signals and reasoning used.
constraints: MUST NOT imply certainty where none exists

ai_governance.decision_authority_rule: The model may suggest. The system must decide. Any output affecting user guidance MUST pass through validation against known taxonomy or rules, constraint to allowed output space, and system-level selection logic. Direct model-to-user decision output is prohibited.

fact_vs_interpretation.facts: Must originate from the data layer. Must be traceable and verifiable.
fact_vs_interpretation.derived_signals: May be computed (rankings, scores). Must be documented and explainable.
fact_vs_interpretation.interpretations: Must be clearly framed as guidance, not truth. Must include rationale and limitations.
prohibited: Model outputs presented as verified conclusions

ontology_policy.rule: Standard ontologies (e.g., SNOMED) are READ-ONLY. Used for normalization, not decision-making.
prohibited: Derive decisions through deep graph traversal
Replace system logic with ontology reasoning
ontology_policy.principle: Ontology provides meaning. System provides action.

requirements: Bounded (limited set of options, not open-ended)
required_patterns: This does not replace professional medical advice…

must: Escalate uncertainty when confidence is low
Default to safety in ambiguous scenarios

logging.purpose: Enable audit, support refinement, ensure accountability

ai_governance.enforcement: Any component violating this policy must be corrected before production release. This policy overrides convenience, speed, and model capability.
ai_governance.final_statement: Fluency is not evidence. Models assist. Systems decide. Data grounds truth.

corporate_policies.name: Provider Neutrality
corporate_policies.policy: ChatHealthy does not accept revenue from, partner with, or enter into financial relationships with health plans, insurance companies, payer networks, provider organizations, PBMs (pharmacy benefit managers), or pharmaceutical companies. The platform must remain neutral across all entities in the care delivery and payment chain. Revenue sources are limited to: (1) consumer subscriptions, and (2) healthcare SaaS/technology vendor partnerships. No entity that delivers, pays for, or intermediates healthcare may be a source of ChatHealthy revenue.
corporate_policies.rationale: Neutrality is a core product principle and a competitive moat. Users must trust that provider recommendations are based on clinical relevance and proximity, not financial relationships. Any revenue from care-chain entities would create real or perceived bias that destroys the product's value proposition.

corporate_policies.name: Single-Tenant Architecture
corporate_policies.policy: ChatHealthy is single-tenant by design. Multi-tenancy is a healthcare anti-pattern and must never be proposed or implemented. Each deployment serves one organization with isolated data.
corporate_policies.rationale: Healthcare data isolation is a compliance requirement and a trust requirement. Multi-tenancy introduces data leakage risk that is unacceptable in healthcare.

corporate_policies.name: IP Protection
corporate_policies.policy: Source code, architecture, and design documents are NOT public by default. Copyright remains with Skip Snow. Credential and secret files are always private. Public exposure of any artifact requires explicit authorization.
corporate_policies.rationale: Supersedes prior 'Public By Default' policy. IP protection is required as the product matures toward funding and licensing. Prior open posture was appropriate for early development but is no longer in effect.

corporate_policies.name: HIPAA Consent Framework
corporate_policies.policy: User data collection follows a two-tier consent flow: (1) verbatim transcript with explicit consent, (2) de-identified summary with explicit consent, (3) contact-only if both declined. Safety audit trail is stored without consent as an operational record. Pending legal review items tracked in brain/pending_legal_questions.json.
corporate_policies.rationale: HIPAA compliance is non-negotiable. The two-tier flow gives users control while enabling business analytics on de-identified data.

corporate_policies.name: Four-Application Boundary
corporate_policies.policy: The system is exactly four applications in two categories. PRODUCT (customer-facing): (1) Static Website on Cloudflare, (2) Chat Window on HuggingFace/Azure, (3) Data Pipelines on Azure Functions. DEVOPS: (4) The Brain — AI-native SDLC operating system (local + Azure, public). Boundaries are strict. Integration only via prescribed patterns: iframe (App1→App2), HTTP POST /api/Router (App2→App3), GPTReader API (Brain→App3). No application may bypass these boundaries.
corporate_policies.rationale: Separation of concerns, independent scaling, and clear ownership. Product applications serve customers. The Brain governs how the product gets built — governance, prompts, plans, assignments, audit trails, manifests. Separating DevOps from product prevents SDLC concerns from leaking into customer-facing code.

corporate_policies.name: Real System Testing
corporate_policies.policy: End-to-end tests use real systems (MongoDB, Anthropic, OpenAI, SparkPost). No mocks in e2e tests. Unit tests may use mocks. Test data is tagged with testdata=true and persisted in the dev database (no teardown).
corporate_policies.rationale: Mock-based tests masked a production migration failure in a prior project. Real system tests catch integration issues that mocks cannot.

corporate_policies.name: Engineering Rules Are Standards
corporate_policies.policy: The engineering operating rules (operating_rules.json) constitute a binding standard. All AI agents and development processes must comply with these rules without exception. Any deviation requires a signed risk acceptance from Skip Snow recorded in the RiskAcceptance pseudo-collection. No agent, workflow, or automation may override, ignore, or work around an engineering rule without this authorization.
corporate_policies.rationale: Engineering rules are learned from real incidents and encode hard-won operational discipline. Treating them as guidelines rather than standards led to repeated violations. Compliance is mandatory, not advisory.

corporate_policies.name: Business Artifacts Gate
corporate_policies.policy: No release to production without completed business artifacts. Required artifacts per release: (1) QA Report PDF with GPT release gate approval, (2) IP License Agreement (current, signed), (3) Business Model (current version). These are business documents, not engineering artifacts. Stored in Azure admin container. Boss owns the checklist.
corporate_policies.rationale: A release is a business event, not just a code event. Business readiness must be demonstrated alongside technical readiness.

corporate_policies.name: Role In System Prompt
corporate_policies.policy: Every AI agent role definition (identity, responsibilities, constraints, governance bindings) must be defined in the system prompt, never in the user prompt. The system prompt is the authoritative source for who the agent is. The user prompt contains only the assignment payload. This enables prompt caching — the static role definition is sent once and reused across assignments.
corporate_policies.rationale: Mixing role definition into user prompts defeats prompt caching, inflates token cost, and creates drift risk where the same agent gets subtly different identities across assignments. Separation of identity (system) from task (user) is a first principle of reliable AI operations.

corporate_policies.name: AI Translates, System Answers
corporate_policies.policy: The AI turns what the user says into a clear question. The system answers using real data, not guesses. The AI's role is translation (natural language to structured intent). The system's role is resolution (query real data, apply rules, return bounded results). The AI must never generate answers from its own knowledge when system data exists to answer the question.
corporate_policies.rationale: This is the operational restatement of GOV-001's core principle ('The model may suggest. The system must decide.') applied specifically to the user-facing chat. Users trust that answers come from verified provider data, not LLM confabulation. Every answer must trace back to the data layer.

implementation_standards.name: System Content Precedence
implementation_standards.standard: When both the system and the AI produce output for the same response, system-generated content takes precedence. Redundant AI content must be stripped. The system summary, counts, links, and structured metadata are authoritative. The AI response retains only non-redundant content (e.g., provider listing, conversational context).
implementation_standards.enforcement: A small model (e.g., Haiku) strips redundant summary/pagination language from the AI response when a system summary_message exists.

implementation_standards.name: User Terms Over Professional Terms
implementation_standards.standard: All user-facing output must use the user's own language, not professional/medical terminology. If the user says 'shrinks', the system says 'shrinks' — not 'psychiatrists'. The AI may translate user terms to professional codes internally for query resolution, but the user-facing response must echo the user's words.
implementation_standards.enforcement: summary_message is built from the user's original message (body.message), not from the LLM's translated tool parameters.

corporate_policies.name: Environment Isolation — No Cross-Environment Data Movement
corporate_policies.policy: Data may only move within its environment chain: dev pipeline → dev frontend, staging pipeline → staging frontend, prod pipeline → prod frontend. No cross-environment copies (e.g., dev → prod, staging → dev). Within the pipeline cluster, data promotes forward only: dev → staging → prod via MigrateEnvironment. No backward migration. No shortcuts. Only Boss can authorize a deviation from this policy — not GPT, not Claude, not any automated process.
corporate_policies.rationale: Environment isolation is a healthcare compliance requirement. Cross-environment data movement creates audit gaps, breaks reproducibility, and risks exposing test data in production or production data in dev. The forward-only promotion chain ensures every dataset in staging was proven in dev, and every dataset in prod was proven in staging.

corporate_policies.name: Design For Today
corporate_policies.policy: We design for today, not the future. It is a fundamental principle of AI-created applications that can be refactored on a dime if the brain's records are rigorously groomed, refactored, and enhanced to increase the usefulness of the brain to function as per design. Speculative architecture, premature abstractions, and designing for hypothetical future requirements are prohibited. Build what is needed now. Refactor when the future actually arrives.

statements.statement: The brain's records must be rigorously groomed, refactored, and enhanced to increase the usefulness of the brain to function as per design.

corporate_policies.rationale: AI collapses the cost of refactoring from weeks to hours. The traditional justification for upfront design — that change is expensive — no longer holds. Speculative architecture is waste. Brain rigor (governance, traceability, tests, groomed records) is what makes cheap refactoring safe. Without rigor, this policy fails.

corporate_policies.name: No Providers In The Room
corporate_policies.policy: Doctors, providers, and licensed clinicians are NEVER participants in a Discuss Care session. The session transcript is shared WITH the doctor after. The doctor is never IN the room.
corporate_policies.rationale: Provider presence creates clinical decision support risk (FDA), malpractice exposure, and transforms the platform from consumer navigation to clinical tool. This boundary is permanent.

corporate_policies.name: Security Disclosure and HIPAA Positioning
corporate_policies.policy: ChatHealthy.ai is NOT a HIPAA covered entity and is NOT subject to HIPAA regulations. We are a consumer navigation platform, not a healthcare provider or business associate. However, we voluntarily adopt enterprise-grade security standards to protect user data.
security_standards: DOD-level security audit standard (FedRAMP or equivalent)
corporate_policies.disclosure_requirement: Every session and every document must disclose: (1) We are not subject to HIPAA. (2) We voluntarily maintain audited security at enterprise healthcare standards. (3) Even if a participant happens to be a licensed provider, the platform remains a consumer tool and does not create a provider-patient relationship.
corporate_policies.rationale: Neutrality requires transparency. We earn trust by choosing to be secure, not by being compelled. This avoids HIPAA regulatory burden while exceeding the security expectations of healthcare buyers.
